_help: HAND-MAINTAINED. scripts/walk_routes.py reads this file and never writes it.
The stops students actually use for a building, where the map gets it
wrong. Without an entry a building is served by its own stop (uNivUS's
table, venues-base.json) and one more stop when the walk to it is barely
longer, both by path distance on OpenStreetMap. Path distance can't see a
climb, a road with no crossing or a door on the far side, so a stop that
is nearer on the map can be the one nobody uses.
Each entry lists stop codes, the usual one first: it becomes the
building's stop for imports and search, and the planner leaves from and
arrives at whichever listed stop is quicker at the time. A stop's twin
across the road comes with it; don't list both. Say why in 'why'.

LT21.why: A path runs straight from LT21 to S17 and LT27. University Hall is nearer on the map but much harder to reach.
